{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_92d8f617a380420a92c50ff6","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Run onError and afterSession when beforeSession throws\n2\t\n3\tIssue: re-cinq/HALEngine#94\n4\tLabels: priority:medium, type:bug, size:S, area:api\n5\t\n6\t## Why\n7\t\n8\t`beforeSession` is awaited before the `try` block opens, so a throw from it escapes before the `catch` and `finally` exist. Neither `onError` nor `afterSession` runs.\n9\t\n10\tThat breaks the guarantee the hook names imply. A deployer who allocates something in `beforeSession` — a span, a database handle, a rate-limit token — and releases it in `afterSession` leaks it on exactly the path where the allocation failed, and learns nothing from `onError` because it never fires. The failure is silent in the engine and visible only as an unexplained rejection at the caller.\n11\t\n12\tRecorded as measured behaviour in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` by HALEngine#83, which scoped itself to specifying the seam rather than changing it, and raised again by the reviewer on that PR. The spec notes this property is owned by no issue in the epic; this is that issue.\n13\t\n14\t## What to do\n15\t\n16\tMove the `beforeSession` call inside the `try`, so a throw from it reaches the same `catch` and `finally` as any other failure in the turn, and decide one question explicitly: whether `afterSession` running after a failed `beforeSession` is what a deployer wants, or whether it needs to know the session never started. Record the answer in the spec either way, because a cleanup hook that cannot tell \"never allocated\" from \"allocated and finished\" is a new trap for the same reader.\n17\t\n18\t## Acceptance criteria\n19\t\n20\t- [ ] A `beforeSession` that throws still reaches the caller as a rejection, unchanged from today\n21\t- [ ] `onError` fires for that throw, with the same argument shape as any other orchestrator failure\n22\t- [ ] `afterSession` fires for that throw, and the spec states what a hook can assume about how much of the turn happened\n23\t- [ ] A non-throwing `beforeSession` behaves exactly as today, pinned by the existing tests remaining unedited\n24\t- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded-flaw line with the new guarantee, and the CHANGELOG says what changes for an existing consumer\n25\t- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass\n26\t\n27\t## Tech notes\n28\t\n29\tKey files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `beforeSession` call above the `try`), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.\n30\t\n31\tOut of scope: the `instanceof Error` gate on `onError` (its own issue) and usage accounting across tool rounds (HALEngine#93).\n32\t\n33\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"413e4093-822e-4255-a152-2fb521364e6e","uuid":"12fae218-6855-4251-8bfd-03e58ef6b93e","timestamp":"2026-11-01T01:38:03.540Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/2276f76deaa8/workspace/ticket.md","content":"# Run onError and afterSession when beforeSession throws\n\nIssue: re-cinq/HALEngine#94\nLabels: priority:medium, type:bug, size:S, area:api\n\n## Why\n\n`beforeSession` is awaited before the `try` block opens, so a throw from it escapes before the `catch` and `finally` exist. Neither `onError` nor `afterSession` runs.\n\nThat breaks the guarantee the hook names imply. A deployer who allocates something in `beforeSession` — a span, a database handle, a rate-limit token — and releases it in `afterSession` leaks it on exactly the path where the allocation failed, and learns nothing from `onError` because it never fires. The failure is silent in the engine and visible only as an unexplained rejection at the caller.\n\nRecorded as measured behaviour in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` by HALEngine#83, which scoped itself to specifying the seam rather than changing it, and raised again by the reviewer on that PR. The spec notes this property is owned by no issue in the epic; this is that issue.\n\n## What to do\n\nMove the `beforeSession` call inside the `try`, so a throw from it reaches the same `catch` and `finally` as any other failure in the turn, and decide one question explicitly: whether `afterSession` running after a failed `beforeSession` is what a deployer wants, or whether it needs to know the session never started. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_a37cea6f264d4b8d951965ca","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Config-Installed Orchestrator Hooks\n2\t\n3\t| Field  | Value                |\n4\t| ------ | -------------------- |\n5\t| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#36 |\n6\t| Status | Shipped              |\n7\t\n8\t`OrchestratorHooks` is the engine's only lifecycle seam, and `HalEngineConfig.orchestrator.hooks` is the supported way to install it: `createHalEngine` forwards the set to `createChatOrchestrator`, so a hook a deployer passes through the factory reaches the running orchestrator rather than sitting unread on the config object. This spec pins that forwarding and the measured semantics the seam already carries, so the hook-based features that follow in this epic — transparency disclosure, audit and usage recording, human oversight, provider failover — specify against real behaviour rather than against what the hook names suggest.\n9\t\n10\t## Installing hooks through config\n11\t\n12\t- A hook passed through `orchestrator.hooks` is forwarded to the orchestrator and fires ([validated by: forwards an orchestrator hook, so one passed through the config actually fires](../../src/config.test.ts#L19)).\n13\t- An engine built with no `orchestrator` key at all still processes a message, so the field is optional in fact and not only in the type ([validated by: processes a message when the config declares no orchestrator key at all](../../src/config.test.ts#L95)).\n14\t- A `beforeModelResponse` hook installed through config is handed the base system prompt built from `prompt`, proving the hook reaches the orchestrator and is wired into the prompt pipeline rather than only being stored on the config ([validated by: hands a config-installed beforeModelResponse hook the built base system prompt, not merely storing it](../../src/config.test.ts#L108)).\n15\t- The value the hook returns then replaces the system prompt the provider receives; this is exercised at the orchestrator layer because `HalEngineConfig.provider` takes a `ProviderConfig` and offers no seam to inject a recording provider through config ([validated by: replaces system prompt with returned value](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L194)).\n16\t- For a session that completes without error the hooks fire in the order `beforeSession` → `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L132)).\n17\t\n18\t## Engine startup\n19\t\n20\t- The engine's `start()` method rejects the returned promise when it cannot bind the configured port, rather than emitting an unhandled error event that would take the process down ([validated by: rejects instead of taking the process down with an unhandled error event](../../src/config.test.ts#L174)).\n21\t\n22\t## Measured semantics — out of scope\n23\t\n24\tThese three properties of `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` are recorded so the hook features that follow specify against real behaviour. This issue changes none of them; each is a separate, out-of-scope change owned by no issue in this epic.\n25\t\n26\t- `beforeSession` is awaited before the `try` block opens ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L91](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L91)), so a throw there escapes before the `catch`/`finally` exist and skips both `onError` and `afterSession`.\n27\t- The `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error` ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L150](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L150)), so a rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string or object — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n28\t- `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L148](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L148)), and is passed the `lastUsage` local — the most recent round's usage, not a sum across tool rounds, so a deployer using the hook for billing or audit under-counts every turn that ran tools.\n29\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"413e4093-822e-4255-a152-2fb521364e6e","uuid":"c79adbe1-375f-47e3-94d4-f0c4d0fa48cc","timestamp":"2026-11-01T01:38:07.325Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/2276f76deaa8/workspace/target/specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md","content":"# Config-Installed Orchestrator Hooks\n\n| Field  | Value                |\n| ------ | -------------------- |\n| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#36 |\n| Status | Shipped              |\n\n`OrchestratorHooks` is the engine's only lifecycle seam, and `HalEngineConfig.orchestrator.hooks` is the supported way to install it: `createHalEngine` forwards the set to `createChatOrchestrator`, so a hook a deployer passes through the factory reaches the running orchestrator rather than sitting unread on the config object. This spec pins that forwarding and the measured semantics the seam already carries, so the hook-based features that follow in this epic — transparency disclosure, audit and usage recording, human oversight, provider failover — specify against real behaviour rather than against what the hook names suggest.\n\n## Installing hooks through config\n\n- A hook passed through `orchestrator.hooks` is forwarded to the orchestrator and fires ([validated by: forwards an orchestrator hook, so one passed through the config actually fires](../../src/config.test.ts#L19)).\n- An engine built with no `orchestrator` key at all still processes a message, so the field is optional in fact and not only in the type ([validated by: processes a message when the config declares no orchestrator key at all](../../src/config.test.ts#L95)).\n- A `beforeModelResponse` hook installed through config is handed the base system prompt built from `prompt`, proving the hook reaches the orchestrator and is wired into the prompt pipeline rather than only being stored on the config ([validated by: hands a config-installed beforeModelResponse hook the built base system prompt, not merely storing it](../../src/config.test.ts#L108)).\n- The value the hook returns then replaces the system prompt the provider receives; this is exercised at the orchestrator layer because `HalEngineConfig.provider` takes a `ProviderConfig` and offers no seam to inject a recording provider through config ([validated by: replaces system prompt with returned value](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L194)).\n- For a session that completes without error the hooks fire in the order `beforeSession` → `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L132)).\n\n## Engine startup\n\n- The engine's `start()` method rejects the returned promise when it cannot bind the configured port, rather than emitting an unhandled error event that would take the process down ([validated by: rejects instead of taking the process down with an unhandled error event](../../src/config.test.ts#L174)).\n\n## Measured semantics — out of scope\n\nThese three properties of `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` are recorded so the hook features that follow specify against real behaviour. This issue changes none of them; each is a separate, out-of-scope change owned by no issue in this epic.\n\n- `beforeSession` is awaited before the `try` block opens ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L91](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L91)), so a throw there escapes before the `catch`/`finally` exist and skips both `onError` and `afterSession`.\n- The `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error` ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L150](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L150)), so a rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string or object — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n- `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L148](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L148)), and is passed the `lastUsage` local — the most recent round's usage, not a sum across tool rounds, so a deployer using the hook for billing or audit under-counts every turn that ran tools.\n","numLines":29,"startLine":1,"totalLines":29}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_a37cea6f264d4b8d951965ca","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_c223eb9eaa3d40b1bb962507","type":"tool_result","content":"1\timport type {ChatSession} from '../types/session.js';\n2\timport type {ToolRegistry, ToolContext, ToolResponse} from './tools/registry.js';\n3\timport type {\n4\t  AIProvider,\n5\t  Message,\n6\t  MessageChunk,\n7\t  SendMessageParams,\n8\t  ToolCall,\n9\t  ToolResultContent,\n10\t  UsageMetadata,\n11\t} from '../types/ai.js';\n12\timport type {OutgoingMessage} from '../types/messages.js';\n13\timport type {PromptBuilder, PromptBuilderOptions} from '../infrastructure/builders/promptBuilder.js';\n14\timport type {SessionStore} from '../types/sessionStore.js';\n15\timport {toMessages, createContextConfig} from './conversationContext.js';\n16\timport type {ContextConfig} from './conversationContext.js';\n17\timport {\n18\t  shouldContinueToolLoop,\n19\t  collectText,\n20\t  buildToolCallMessages,\n21\t  collectToolCalls,\n22\t  extractStopReason,\n23\t  extractUsage,\n24\t} from './orchestratorHelpers.js';\n25\timport {appendEntry, commitStreamingEntries} from './entryMutations.js';\n26\timport {log} from '../shared/logger.js';\n27\t\n28\tconst DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 5;\n29\t\n30\texport interface OrchestratorHooks {\n31\t  beforeSession?: (session: ChatSession) => Promise<void>;\n32\t  afterSession?: (session: ChatSession) => Promise<void>;\n33\t  beforeUserInput?: (session: ChatSession, userMessage: string) => Promise<string>;\n34\t  afterUserInput?: (session: ChatSession, userMessage: string) => Promise<void>;\n35\t  beforeModelResponse?: (session: ChatSession, systemPrompt: string) => Promise<string>;\n36\t  afterModelResponse?: (session: ChatSession, responseText: string, usage?: UsageMetadata) => Promise<void>;\n37\t  onError?: (session: ChatSession, error: Error) => Promise<void>;\n38\t  /** The supported seam for an EU AI Act Art. 14 human-oversight control: fires before each known tool's executor, and a returned ToolResponse replaces the call (see docs/adding-a-tool.md); it receives the model's raw tool input and, through session, the caller's authHeaders, so a policy that logs either logs personal data and credential material; the engine asserts nothing about any policy installed here. */\n39\t  beforeToolCall?: (session: ChatSession, call: ToolCall) => Promise<ToolResponse | undefined>;\n40\t  /** Fires when the model asks for a tool round the budget refuses, after the last provider call and before afterModelResponse; a returned string reaches the user as the turn's closing text, and the engine writes none of its own (see specs/hal-engine-tool-budget/spec.md). */\n41\t  onToolBudgetExhausted?: (session: ChatSession, budget: ToolBudgetInfo) => Promise<string | undefined>;\n42\t}\n43\t\n44\texport interface ToolBudgetInfo {\n45\t  maxToolRounds: number;\n46\t  requestedTools: string[];\n47\t}\n48\t\n49\ttype BeforeToolCall = NonNullable<OrchestratorHooks['beforeToolCall']>;\n50\ttype OnToolBudgetExhausted = NonNullable<OrchestratorHooks['onToolBudgetExhausted']>;\n51\t\n52\texport const TOOL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED = 'tool_budget_exhausted';\n53\t\n54\texport interface ChatOrchestrator {\n55\t  processMessage(session: ChatSession): Promise<string>;\n56\t  processMessageStream(session: ChatSession): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk>;\n57\t}\n58\t\n59\texport interface ChatOrchestratorOptions {\n60\t  maxToolRounds?: number;\n61\t  contextConfig?: Partial<ContextConfig>;\n62\t  promptBuilderOptions?: PromptBuilderOptions;\n63\t  hooks?: OrchestratorHooks;\n64\t  sessionStore?: SessionStore;\n65\t}\n66\t\n67\tinterface ToolExecutionResult {\n68\t  clientMessages: OutgoingMessage[];\n69\t  suppressOutput: boolean;\n70\t}\n71\texport function createChatOrchestrator(\n72\t  provider: AIProvider,\n73\t  promptBuilder: PromptBuilder,\n74\t  toolRegistry?: ToolRegistry,\n75\t  options?: ChatOrchestratorOptions\n76\t): ChatOrchestrator {\n77\t  const maxToolRounds = normalizeToolRounds(options?.maxToolRounds);\n78\t  const contextConfig = createContextConfig(options?.contextConfig);\n79\t  const toolInstructions = toolRegistry?.getPromptInstructions();\n80\t  const baseSystemPrompt = promptBuilder.build({...options?.promptBuilderOptions, toolInstructions});\n81\t  const tools = toolRegistry?.getDefinitions();\n82\t  const hooks = options?.hooks;\n83\t  const sessionStore = options?.sessionStore;\n84\t\n85\t  return {\n86\t    async processMessage(session: ChatSession): Promise<string> {\n87\t      return collectText(this.processMessageStream(session));\n88\t    },\n89\t\n90\t    async *processMessageStream(session: ChatSession): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n91\t      if (hooks?.beforeSession) await hooks.beforeSession(session);\n92\t\n93\t      try {\n94\t        let userMessage = lastUserContent(session);\n95\t\n96\t        if (hooks?.beforeUserInput) {\n97\t          userMessage = await rewriteUserMessage(session, userMessage, hooks.beforeUserInput);\n98\t        }\n99\t\n100\t        if (hooks?.afterUserInput) await hooks.afterUserInput(session, userMessage);\n101\t\n102\t        const systemPrompt = hooks?.beforeModelResponse\n103\t          ? await hooks.beforeModelResponse(session, baseSystemPrompt)\n104\t          : baseSystemPrompt;\n105\t\n106\t        const messages: Message[] = toMessages(session.entries, contextConfig);\n107\t        let lastUsage: UsageMetadata | undefined;\n108\t        let responseText = '';\n109\t\n110\t        // Bounded by the budget gate below, not the header: maxToolRounds executed rounds, maxToolRounds + 1 provider calls.\n111\t        for (let round = 0; ; round++) {\n112\t          log.info('orchestrator', 'starting round', {round});\n113\t          const pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[] = [];\n114\t\n115\t          const outcome = yield* streamRound(provider, {messages, systemPrompt, tools}, pendingToolCalls);\n116\t          responseText += outcome.text;\n117\t          lastUsage = outcome.usage ?? lastUsage;\n118\t\n119\t          if (!shouldContinueToolLoop(outcome.stopReason, pendingToolCalls, toolRegistry)) break;\n120\t          if (budgetSpent(round, maxToolRounds, pendingToolCalls)) {\n121\t            const budget = {maxToolRounds, requestedTools: pendingToolCalls.map(tc => tc.name)};\n122\t            responseText += yield* closeExhaustedTurn(session, budget, hooks?.onToolBudgetExhausted);\n123\t            break;\n124\t          }\n125\t\n126\t          log.info('orchestrator', 'executing tools', {tools: pendingToolCalls.map(tc => tc.name)});\n127\t          const {clientMessages, suppressOutput} = await executeToolCalls(\n128\t            pendingToolCalls,\n129\t            messages,\n130\t            session,\n131\t            toolCallRunner(toolRegistry!, session, hooks?.beforeToolCall)\n132\t          );\n133\t          log.info('orchestrator', 'tool execution complete', {\n134\t            clientMessageCount: clientMessages.length,\n135\t            clientMessageTypes: clientMessages.map(m => m.type),\n136\t            suppressOutput,\n137\t          });\n138\t\n139\t          if (clientMessages.length > 0) {\n140\t            yield {type: 'tool_result' as const, clientMessages};\n141\t          }\n142\t\n143\t          if (suppressOutput) {\n144\t            yield {type: 'suppress_output' as const};\n145\t          }\n146\t        }\n147\t\n148\t        if (hooks?.afterModelResponse) await hooks.afterModelResponse(session, responseText, lastUsage);\n149\t      } catch (error) {\n150\t        if (hooks?.onError && error instanceof Error) {\n151\t          await hooks.onError(session, error);\n152\t        }\n153\t        throw error;\n154\t      } finally {\n155\t        // Before both: a provider that threw mid-stream leaves an entry open, and nothing should persist it that way.\n156\t        commitStreamingEntries(session);\n157\t        try {\n158\t          if (hooks?.afterSession) await hooks.afterSession(session);\n159\t        } finally {\n160\t          await saveSession(sessionStore, session);\n161\t        }\n162\t      }\n163\t    },\n164\t  };\n165\t}\n166\t\n167\t// A negative budget means no tool rounds; a non-finite one, NaN included, falls back to the default rather than never ending.\n168\tfunction normalizeToolRounds(value: number | undefined): number {\n169\t  if (value === undefined || !Number.isFinite(value)) return DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS;\n170\t  return Math.max(0, Math.floor(value));\n171\t}\n172\t\n173\t// Gates execution, not the provider call: a round nobody can read is never run, and the call that read the last one already has.\n174\tfunction budgetSpent(round: number, maxToolRounds: number, pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[]): boolean {\n175\t  if (round < maxToolRounds) return false;\n176\t  log.warn('orchestrator', 'tool budget exhausted', {\n177\t    maxToolRounds,\n178\t    requestedTools: pendingToolCalls.map(tc => tc.name),\n179\t  });\n180\t  return true;\n181\t}\n182\t\n183\t// The stop always follows the text: the round's own stop already committed its entry, and a bare text chunk would open one never committed.\n184\tasync function* closeExhaustedTurn(\n185\t  session: ChatSession,\n186\t  budget: ToolBudgetInfo,\n187\t  hook?: OnToolBudgetExhausted\n188\t): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk, string> {\n189\t  const sentence = (hook ? await hook(session, budget) : undefined) ?? '';\n190\t  if (sentence !== '') yield {type: 'text', text: sentence};\n191\t  yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: TOOL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED};\n192\t  return sentence;\n193\t}\n194\t\n195\tinterface RoundOutcome {\n196\t  stopReason: string;\n197\t  text: string;\n198\t  usage?: UsageMetadata;\n199\t}\n200\t\n201\t// `yield*` in the caller evaluates to this return, so the round's totals come back as data.\n202\tasync function* streamRound(\n203\t  provider: AIProvider,\n204\t  request: SendMessageParams,\n205\t  pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[]\n206\t): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk, RoundOutcome> {\n207\t  let stopReason = '';\n208\t  let text = '';\n209\t  let usage: UsageMetadata | undefined;\n210\t\n211\t  for await (const chunk of provider.sendMessage(request)) {\n212\t    yield chunk;\n213\t    collectToolCalls(chunk, pendingToolCalls);\n214\t    stopReason = extractStopReason(chunk) ?? stopReason;\n215\t    usage = extractUsage(chunk) ?? usage;\n216\t    if (chunk.type === 'text') text += chunk.text;\n217\t  }\n218\t\n219\t  return {stopReason, text, usage};\n220\t}\n221\t\n222\t// A changed message is also written back to the session's last user entry.\n223\tasync function rewriteUserMessage(\n224\t  session: ChatSession,\n225\t  userMessage: string,\n226\t  hook: (session: ChatSession, userMessage: string) => Promise<string>\n227\t): Promise<string> {\n228\t  const modified = await hook(session, userMessage);\n229\t  if (modified === userMessage) return userMessage;\n230\t\n231\t  updateLastUserContent(session, modified);\n232\t  return modified;\n233\t}\n234\t\n235\tfunction lastUserContent(session: ChatSession): string {\n236\t  for (let i = session.entries.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {\n237\t    const entry = session.entries[i];\n238\t    if (entry.role === 'user') return entry.content;\n239\t  }\n240\t  return '';\n241\t}\n242\t\n243\tfunction updateLastUserContent(session: ChatSession, content: string): void {\n244\t  for (let i = session.entries.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {\n245\t    const entry = session.entries[i];\n246\t    if (entry.role === 'user') {\n247\t      entry.content = content;\n248\t      return;\n249\t    }\n250\t  }\n251\t}\n252\t\n253\t// One runner per round: the policy sees each known call before its executor, and an unknown name keeps the registry's own path.\n254\tfunction toolCallRunner(toolRegistry: ToolRegistry, session: ChatSession, beforeToolCall?: BeforeToolCall) {\n255\t  const context: ToolContext = {\n256\t    userId: session.userId,\n257\t    sessionId: session.sessionId,\n258\t    workspaceId: session.workspaceId,\n259\t    authHeaders: session.authHeaders,\n260\t  };\n261\t\n262\t  return async (tc: ToolCall): Promise<ToolResponse> => {\n263\t    const declined =\n264\t      beforeToolCall && toolRegistry.has(tc.name) ? await consultPolicy(beforeToolCall, session, tc) : undefined;\n265\t    return declined ?? toolRegistry.execute(tc.name, tc.input, context);\n266\t  };\n267\t}\n268\t\n269\t// A throwing policy declines its call rather than failing the turn: every tool_use must still be answered.\n270\tasync function consultPolicy(\n271\t  policy: BeforeToolCall,\n272\t  session: ChatSession,\n273\t  tc: ToolCall\n274\t): Promise<ToolResponse | undefined> {\n275\t  try {\n276\t    return await policy(session, tc);\n277\t  } catch (error) {\n278\t    log.warn('orchestrator', 'beforeToolCall threw, so the call is declined', {\n279\t      tool: tc.name,\n280\t      errorType: error instanceof Error ? type {ChatSession} from '../types/session.js';\nimport type {ToolRegistry, ToolContext, ToolResponse} from './tools/registry.js';\nimport type {\n  AIProvider,\n  Message,\n  MessageChunk,\n  SendMessageParams,\n  ToolCall,\n  ToolResultContent,\n  UsageMetadata,\n} from '../types/ai.js';\nimport type {OutgoingMessage} from '../types/messages.js';\nimport type {PromptBuilder, PromptBuilderOptions} from '../infrastructure/builders/promptBuilder.js';\nimport type {SessionStore} from '../types/sessionStore.js';\nimport {toMessages, createContextConfig} from './conversationContext.js';\nimport type {ContextConfig} from './conversationContext.js';\nimport {\n  shouldContinueToolLoop,\n  collectText,\n  buildToolCallMessages,\n  collectToolCalls,\n  extractStopReason,\n  extractUsage,\n} from './orchestratorHelpers.js';\nimport {appendEntry, commitStreamingEntries} from './entryMutations.js';\nimport {log} from '../shared/logger.js';\n\nconst DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 5;\n\nexport interface OrchestratorHooks {\n  beforeSession?: (session: ChatSession) => Promise<void>;\n  afterSession?: (session: ChatSession) => Promise<void>;\n  beforeUserInput?: (session: ChatSession, userMessage: string) => Promise<string>;\n  afterUserInput?: (session: ChatSession, userMessage: string) => Promise<void>;\n  beforeModelResponse?: (session: ChatSession, systemPrompt: string) => Promise<string>;\n  afterModelResponse?: (session: ChatSession, responseText: string, usage?: UsageMetadata) => Promise<void>;\n  onError?: (session: ChatSession, error: Error) => Promise<void>;\n  /** The supported seam for an EU AI Act Art. 14 human-oversight control: fires before each known tool's executor, and a returned ToolResponse replaces the call (see docs/adding-a-tool.md); it receives the model's raw tool input and, through session, the caller's authHeaders, so a policy that logs either logs personal data and credential material; the engine asserts nothing about any policy installed here. */\n  beforeToolCall?: (session: ChatSession, call: ToolCall) => Promise<ToolResponse | undefined>;\n  /** Fires when the model asks for a tool round the budget refuses, after the last provider call and before afterModelResponse; a returned string reaches the user as the turn's closing text, and the engine writes none of its own (see specs/hal-engine-tool-budget/spec.md). */\n  onToolBudgetExhausted?: (session: ChatSession, budget: ToolBudgetInfo) => Promise<string | undefined>;\n}\n\nexport interface ToolBudgetInfo {\n  maxToolRounds: number;\n  requestedTools: string[];\n}\n\ntype BeforeToolCall = NonNullable<OrchestratorHooks['beforeToolCall']>;\ntype OnToolBudgetExhausted = NonNullable<OrchestratorHooks['onToolBudgetExhausted']>;\n\nexport const TOOL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED = 'tool_budget_exhausted';\n\nexport interface ChatOrchestrator {\n  processMessage(session: ChatSession): Promise<string>;\n  processMessageStream(session: ChatSession): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk>;\n}\n\nexport interface ChatOrchestratorOptions {\n  maxToolRounds?: number;\n  contextConfig?: Partial<ContextConfig>;\n  promptBuilderOptions?: PromptBuilderOptions;\n  hooks?: OrchestratorHooks;\n  sessionStore?: SessionStore;\n}\n\ninterface ToolExecutionResult {\n  clientMessages: OutgoingMessage[];\n  suppressOutput: boolean;\n}\nexport function createChatOrchestrator(\n  provider: AIProvider,\n  promptBuilder: PromptBuilder,\n  toolRegistry?: ToolRegistry,\n  options?: ChatOrchestratorOptions\n): ChatOrchestrator {\n  const maxToolRounds = normalizeToolRounds(options?.maxToolRounds);\n  const contextConfig = createContextConfig(options?.contextConfig);\n  const toolInstructions = toolRegistry?.getPromptInstructions();\n  const baseSystemPrompt = promptBuilder.build({...options?.promptBuilderOptions, toolInstructions});\n  const tools = toolRegistry?.getDefinitions();\n  const hooks = options?.hooks;\n  const sessionStore = options?.sessionStore;\n\n  return {\n    async processMessage(session: ChatSession): Promise<string> {\n      return collectText(this.processMessageStream(session));\n    },\n\n    async *processMessageStream(session: ChatSession): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n      if (hooks?.beforeSession) await hooks.beforeSession(session);\n\n      try {\n        let userMessage = lastUserContent(session);\n\n        if (hooks?.beforeUserInput) {\n          userMessage = await rewriteUserMessage(session, userMessage, hooks.beforeUserInput);\n        }\n\n        if (hooks?.afterUserInput) await hooks.afterUserInput(session, userMessage);\n\n        const systemPrompt = hooks?.beforeModelResponse\n          ? await hooks.beforeModelResponse(session, baseSystemPrompt)\n          : baseSystemPrompt;\n\n        const messages: Message[] = toMessages(session.entries, contextConfig);\n        let lastUsage: UsageMetadata | undefined;\n        let responseText = '';\n\n        // Bounded by the budget gate below, not the header: maxToolRounds executed rounds, maxToolRounds + 1 provider calls.\n        for (let round = 0; ; round++) {\n          log.info('orchestrator', 'starting round', {round});\n          const pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[] = [];\n\n          const outcome = yield* streamRound(provider, {messages, systemPrompt, tools}, pendingToolCalls);\n          responseText += outcome.text;\n          lastUsage = outcome.usage ?? lastUsage;\n\n          if (!shouldContinueToolLoop(outcome.stopReason, pendingToolCalls, toolRegistry)) break;\n          if (budgetSpent(round, maxToolRounds, pendingToolCalls)) {\n            const budget = {maxToolRounds, requestedTools: pendingToolCalls.map(tc => tc.name)};\n            responseText += yield* closeExhaustedTurn(session, budget, hooks?.onToolBudgetExhausted);\n            break;\n          }\n\n          log.info('orchestrator', 'executing tools', {tools: pendingToolCalls.map(tc => tc.name)});\n          const {clientMessages, suppressOutput} = await executeToolCalls(\n            pendingToolCalls,\n            messages,\n            session,\n            toolCallRunner(toolRegistry!, session, hooks?.beforeToolCall)\n          );\n          log.info('orchestrator', 'tool execution complete', {\n            clientMessageCount: clientMessages.length,\n            clientMessageTypes: clientMessages.map(m => m.type),\n            suppressOutput,\n          });\n\n          if (clientMessages.length > 0) {\n            yield {type: 'tool_result' as const, clientMessages};\n          }\n\n          if (suppressOutput) {\n            yield {type: 'suppress_output' as const};\n          }\n        }\n\n        if (hooks?.afterModelResponse) await hooks.afterModelResponse(session, responseText, lastUsage);\n      } catch (error) {\n        if (hooks?.onError && error instanceof Error) {\n          await hooks.onError(session, error);\n        }\n        throw error;\n      } finally {\n        // Before both: a provider that threw mid-stream leaves an entry open, and nothing should persist it that way.\n        commitStreamingEntries(session);\n        try {\n          if (hooks?.afterSession) await hooks.afterSession(session);\n        } finally {\n          await saveSession(sessionStore, session);\n        }\n      }\n    },\n  };\n}\n\n// A negative budget means no tool rounds; a non-finite one, NaN included, falls back to the default rather than never ending.\nfunction normalizeToolRounds(value: number | undefined): number {\n  if (value === undefined || !Number.isFinite(value)) return DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS;\n  return Math.max(0, Math.floor(value));\n}\n\n// Gates execution, not the provider call: a round nobody can read is never run, and the call that read the last one already has.\nfunction budgetSpent(round: number, maxToolRounds: number, pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[]): boolean {\n  if (round < maxToolRounds) return false;\n  log.warn('orchestrator', 'tool budget exhausted', {\n    maxToolRounds,\n    requestedTools: pendingToolCalls.map(tc => tc.name),\n  });\n  return true;\n}\n\n// The stop always follows the text: the round's own stop already committed its entry, and a bare text chunk would open one never committed.\nasync function* closeExhaustedTurn(\n  session: ChatSession,\n  budget: ToolBudgetInfo,\n  hook?: OnToolBudgetExhausted\n): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk, string> {\n  const sentence = (hook ? await hook(session, budget) : undefined) ?? '';\n  if (sentence !== '') yield {type: 'text', text: sentence};\n  yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: TOOL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED};\n  return sentence;\n}\n\ninterface RoundOutcome {\n  stopReason: string;\n  text: string;\n  usage?: UsageMetadata;\n}\n\n// `yield*` in the caller evaluates to this return, so the round's totals come back as data.\nasync function* streamRound(\n  provider: AIProvider,\n  request: SendMessageParams,\n  pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[]\n): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk, RoundOutcome> {\n  let stopReason = '';\n  let text = '';\n  let usage: UsageMetadata | undefined;\n\n  for await (const chunk of provider.sendMessage(request)) {\n    yield chunk;\n    collectToolCalls(chunk, pendingToolCalls);\n    stopReason = extractStopReason(chunk) ?? stopReason;\n    usage = extractUsage(chunk) ?? usage;\n    if (chunk.type === 'text') text += chunk.text;\n  }\n\n  return {stopReason, text, usage};\n}\n\n// A changed message is also written back to the session's last user entry.\nasync function rewriteUserMessage(\n  session: ChatSession,\n  userMessage: string,\n  hook: (session: ChatSession, userMessage: string) => Promise<string>\n): Promise<string> {\n  const modified = await hook(session, userMessage);\n  if (modified === userMessage) return userMessage;\n\n  updateLastUserContent(session, modified);\n  return modified;\n}\n\nfunction lastUserContent(session: ChatSession): string {\n  for (let i = session.entries.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {\n    const entry = session.entries[i];\n    if (entry.role === 'user') return entry.content;\n  }\n  return '';\n}\n\nfunction updateLastUserContent(session: ChatSession, content: string): void {\n  for (let i = session.entries.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {\n    const entry = session.entries[i];\n    if (entry.role === 'user') {\n      entry.content = content;\n      return;\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n// One runner per round: the policy sees each known call before its executor, and an unknown name keeps the registry's own path.\nfunction toolCallRunner(toolRegistry: ToolRegistry, session: ChatSession, beforeToolCall?: BeforeToolCall) {\n  const context: ToolContext = {\n    userId: session.userId,\n    sessionId: session.sessionId,\n    workspaceId: session.workspaceId,\n    authHeaders: session.authHeaders,\n  };\n\n  return async (tc: ToolCall): Promise<ToolResponse> => {\n    const declined =\n      beforeToolCall && toolRegistry.has(tc.name) ? await consultPolicy(beforeToolCall, session, tc) : undefined;\n    return declined ?? toolRegistry.execute(tc.name, tc.input, context);\n  };\n}\n\n// A throwing policy declines its call rather than failing the turn: every tool_use must still be answered.\nasync function consultPolicy(\n  policy: BeforeToolCall,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  tc: ToolCall\n): Promise<ToolResponse | undefined> {\n  try {\n    return await policy(session, tc);\n  } catch (error) {\n    log.warn('orchestrator', 'beforeToolCall threw, so the call is declined', {\n      tool: tc.name,\n      errorType: error instanceof Error ? error.name : typeof error,\n    });\n    return {result: `The ${tc.name} call was declined and not performed.`};\n  }\n}\n\nasync function executeToolCalls(\n  pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[],\n  messages: Message[],\n  session: ChatSession,\n  runToolCall: (tc: ToolCall) => Promise<ToolResponse>\n): Promise<ToolExecutionResult> {\n  messages.push(buildToolCallMessages(pendingToolCalls));\n\n  const responses = await Promise.all(\n    pendingToolCalls.map(async tc => {\n      const response = await runToolCall(tc);\n      return {tc, response};\n    })\n  );\n\n  const toolResults: ToolResultContent[] = responses.map(({tc, response}) => ({\n    type: 'tool_result' as const,\n    toolUseId: tc.id,\n    content: response.result,\n  }));\n  messages.push({role: 'user', content: toolResults});\n\n  const rawClientMessages = responses.flatMap(({response}) => response.clientMessages ?? []);\n\n  return {\n    clientMessages: assignEntryIndices(rawClientMessages, session),\n    suppressOutput: responses.some(({response}) => response.suppressAssistantResponse === true),\n  };\n}\n\nfunction assignEntryIndices(clientMessages: OutgoingMessage[], session: ChatSession): OutgoingMessage[] {\n  return clientMessages.map(msg => {\n    if (msg.type !== 'entry_upsert') return msg;\n    const index = appendEntry(session, msg.entry);\n    return {...msg, index};\n  });\n}\n\n// A store outage is not a reason to fail the turn the customer already received.\nasync function saveSession(store: SessionStore | undefined, session: ChatSession): Promise<void> {\n  if (!store?.save) return;\n\n  try {\n    await store.save(session);\n  } catch (error) {\n    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);\n    log.error('orchestrator', 'session save failed', {sessionId: session.sessionId, error: message});\n  }\n}\n","numLines":335,"startLine":1,"totalLines":335}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_c223eb9eaa3d40b1bb962507","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_501cf0a4e1d3488a9ca624f6","type":"tool_result","content":"test-commands.yml\n# Lore test-command interface (lore_list_tests / lore_run_test).\n# Written for this repo's Jest suite rather than adapted from the Vitest\n# equivalent for a Vitest suite: the report shapes happen to match, but the\n# invocations do not.\n- id: hal-engine-jest\n  name: HAL Engine Jest suite\n  cwd: .\n  description: >-\n    The ts-jest unit suite over src/ and scripts/ (jest.config.js roots), run\n    on every pull request in .github/workflows/ci.yml as the \"Test\" step.\n    Selectors are \"<repo-relative-file>::<full test name>\" as emitted by the\n    list command. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_63a26cf30e884e8981ea2f15","type":"tool_result","content":"60\tand the changelog check.\n61\t\n62\tTwo further CI jobs are worth running locally before a release or a change that\n63\ttouches packaging: `npm run check:build-chain` (audit and action pins) and\n64\t`npm run smoke` (packs the tarball and installs it outside this tree).\n65\t\n66\t## Spec Header Table\n67\t\n68\tEvery `specs/*/spec.md` opens with its title, then a two-column header table,\n69\tand carries a lead paragraph of prose before its first `##` section:\n70\t\n71\t```markdown\n72\t# <spec title>\n73\t\n74\t| Field  | Value                  |\n75\t| ------ | ---------------------- |\n76\t| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#<n> |\n77\t| Status | Draft                  |\n78\t\n79\t<lead paragraph>\n80\t```\n81\t\n82\tThe lead paragraph does not have to sit immediately after the table: a spec\n83\tcarrying a metadata block of its own may place that block between the two. What\n84\tthe convention requires is that prose, rather than a section heading, follows\n85\tthe header material, and that the prose runs to at least 40 characters -\n86\tanything shorter is reported as no lead paragraph at all.\n87\t\n88\t`Issue` names the issue the spec was written against, or `n/a` for the specs\n89\tthat predate this convention.\n90\t\n91\t`Status` is one of `Draft`, `In Progress` or `Shipped`. It is not a mood, and\n92\tit is not a claim about how finished the feature is: it is the spec's own\n93\ttest-citation coverage. No testable statement cited is `Draft`, some cited is\n94\t`In Progress`, all cited is `Shipped`. A spec describing shipped, working\n95\tbehaviour still reads `Draft` until its statements cite the tests that\n96\tvalidate them.\n97\t\n98\tA spec that should no longer be graded takes a terminal value instead. The\n99\tparser buckets roughly sixteen labels into five buckets, and the two terminal\n100\tones skip the coverage check whatever the citation count:\n101\t\n102\t| Written into the spec                                            | Bucket                       |\n103\t| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |\n104\t| `Draft`                                                          | `draft`                      |\n105\t| `In Progress`, `In Review`, `Planning`, `WIP`, `Proposed`        | `in-progress`                |\n106\t| `Shipped`, `Implemented`, `Complete`, `Accepted`, `Done`, `Live` | `shipped`                    |\n107\t| `Retired`, `Superseded`, `Removed`, `Deprecated`, `Obsolete`     | `retired` - skips the check  |\n108\t| `Rejected`, `Abandoned`                                          | `rejected` - skips the check |\n109\t\n110\tPrefer the canonical `Draft` / `In Progress` / `Shipped` for a live spec; reach\n111\tfor `Retired` or `Rejected` rather than leaving a superseded spec to claim a\n112\tcoverage tier it will never earn.\n113\t\n114\tADRs do not carry this table. They declare their state as YAML frontmatter\n115\t`status:` instead - `accepted` for a decision the code implements, `proposed`\n116\tfor one it does not. That field does mean maturity, which the spec `Status` row\n117\texplicitly does not. The difference is deliberate: ADRs are exempt from the\n118\tcoverage tier, because asking a decision record to cite a test for every\n119\tstatement it makes is the wrong ask of a decision record.\n120\t\n121\t`.specify/spec.md` is exempt from this section. The exemption covers the header table\n125\tand the lead paragraph only: the Lore coverage job does scan\n126\t`.specify/spec.md`, so link placement still applies to it.\n127\t\n128\t## Spec Test Links\n129\t\n130\tStatements in `specs/*/spec.md` cite their validating test in a trailing\n131\tparenthetical at the end of the statement, where a list item counts as one\n132\tstatement and a paragraph counts per sentence. Tests live beside their source\n133\tin this repo, so the path points into `src/`:\n134\t\n135\t```markdown\n136\t- All entries within a single assistant response are committed before the next\n137\t  user message is processed\n138\t  ([validated by: commits every entry before the next user message](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L42)).\n139\t```\n140\t\n141\tThe citation carries the test's **name** as well as its line. The name is what the\n142\tauthor cited; the line is a derived pointer, and it goes stale on its own - adding\n143\tan import above a suite moves every test below it, and the citation lands on a\n144\tdifferent, still-valid declaration without anything noticing. `npm run spec:names`\n145\tholds each citation to the test it names, and `npm run spec:names:fix` repoints the\n146\tline from the name. The `#Lnn` stays because the lint rule and the coverage job\n147\tboth index by it; a citation without one marks the whole file covered rather than\n148\tone test.\n149\t\n150\tA citation counts as coverage only where it is trailing, and a test link placed\n151\tanywhere else in the statement is a misplaced citation rather than a weaker one.\n152\tUpstream `check:spec-links` reports it and exits 1, and the coverage job that\n153\tconsumes these specs records nothing for it - so a spec can read as fully cited while its coverage is\n154\tzero. A mid-statement link to something that is not a test file - a script, a\n155\tdoc, another spec - is ordinary prose, is never reported, and was never coverage\n156\tto begin with. a value rather than a matcher.\nconst outcomeOf = (call: Promise<unknown>): Promise<string> =>\n  call.then(() => 'resolved without throwing').catch((error: Error) => error.message);\n\nfunction createSession(content: string): ChatSession {\n  return {\n    sessionId: 's1',\n    userId: 'u1',\n    entries: [{role: 'user', content, timestamp: SENT_AT}],\n  };\n}\n\nfunction createMockProvider(response: string, usage?: UsageMetadata): AIProvider {\n  return {\n    async *sendMessage(_params: SendMessageParams): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n      yield {type: 'text', text: response};\n      yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn', usage};\n    },\n    async generateStructured<T>(): Promise<T> {\n      return {} as T;\n    },\n  };\n}\n\nfunction createErrorProvider(error: Error): AIProvider {\n  return {\n    // eslint-disable-next-line require-yield\n    async *sendMessage(): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n      throw error;\n    },\n    async generateStructured<T>(): Promise<T> {\n      return {} as T;\n    },\n  };\n}\n\nconst promptBuilder = new PromptBuilder({identity: 'You are a test assistant.'});\n\ntype RecordedHook =\n  | 'beforeSession'\n  | 'beforeUserInput'\n  | 'afterUserInput'\n  | 'beforeModelResponse'\n  | 'afterModelResponse'\n  | 'afterSession'\n  | 'onError';\n\n// Only the named hooks are installed: one that merely exists changes the observed order.\nconst recordingHooks = (callOrder: string[], names: RecordedHook[]): OrchestratorHooks => {\n  const all: Required<Pick<OrchestratorHooks, RecordedHook>> = {\n    beforeSession: async () => void callOrder.push('beforeSession'),\n    beforeUserInput: async (_session, msg) => {\n      callOrder.push('beforeUserInput');\n      return msg;\n    },\n    afterUserInput: async () => void callOrder.push('afterUserInput'),\n    beforeModelResponse: async (_session, systemPrompt) => {\n      callOrder.push('beforeModelResponse');\n      return systemPrompt;\n    },\n    afterModelResponse: async () => void callOrder.push('afterModelResponse'),\n    afterSession: async () => void callOrder.push('afterSession'),\n    onError: async () => void callOrder.push('onError'),\n  };\n\n  return Object.fromEntries(names.map(name => [name, all[name]])) as OrchestratorHooks;\n};\n\n// Records what the orchestrator actually sent, for tests that assert on the request.\nconst capturingProvider = (): {provider: AIProvider; sent: {systemPrompt: string; lastUserContent: string}} => {\n  const sent = {systemPrompt: '', lastUserContent: ''};\n\n  return {\n    sent,\n    provider: {\n      async *sendMessage(params: SendMessageParams): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n        sent.systemPrompt = params.systemPrompt;\n        const last = params.messages[params.messages.length - 1];\n        sent.lastUserContent = typeof last.content === 'string' ? last.content : '';\n        yield {type: 'text', text: 'ok'};\n        yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn'};\n      },\n      async generateStructured<T>(): Promise<T> {\n        return {} as T;\n      },\n    },\n  };\n};\n\ndescribe('ChatOrchestrator hooks', () => {\n  describe('beforeSession', () => {\n    it('called before anything else', async () => {\n      const callOrder: string[] = [];\n      const hooks = recordingHooks(callOrder, ['beforeSession', 'beforeUserInput', 'beforeModelResponse']);\n\n      const orchestrator = createChatOrchestrator(createMockProvider('hi'), promptBuilder, undefined, {hooks});\n      await orchestrator.processMessage(createSession('hello'));\n\n      expect(callOrder[0]).toBe('beforeSession');\n    });\n  });\n\n  describe('afterSession', () => {\n    it('called after everything createChatOrchestrator(createMockProvider('hi'), promptBuilder, undefined, {hooks});\n      await orchestrator.processMessage(createSession('hello'));\n\n      expect(callOrder).toEqual(['afterModelResponse', 'afterSession']);\n    });\n\n    it('called even when an error occurs', async () => {\n      let afterSessionCalled = false;\n      const hooks: describe('beforeUserInput', () => {\n    it('receives the last user message content', async () => {\n      let receivedMessage = '';\n      const hooks: OrchestratorHooks = {\n        beforeUserInput: async (_session, userMessage) => {\n          receivedMessage = userMessage;\n          return userMessage;\n        },\n      };\n\n      const orchestrator = createChatOrchestrator(createMockProvider('ok'), promptBuilder, undefined, {hooks});\n      await orchestrator.processMessage(createSession('my answer'));\n\n      expect(receivedMessage).toBe('my Detect-only: which assertions merge into one\n * object and which become their own test is the author's call.\n */\nconst TEST_ROOTS = new Set([\"it\", \"test\"]);\nconst TEST_MODIFIERS = new Set([\"only\", \"skip\", \"each\", \"concurrent\"]);\nfunction isTestRoot(node) {\n    return node.type === \"Identifier\" && TEST_ROOTS.has(node.name);\n}\nfunction isTestModifier(node) {\n    return (node.type === \"MemberExpression\" &&\n        !node.computed &&\n        isTestRoot(node.object) &&\n        TEST_MODIFIERS.has(node.property.name));\n}\nfunction isTestCall(node) {\n    const { callee } = node;\n    if (isTestRoot(callee) || isTestModifier(callee)) {\n        return true;\n    }\n    // it.each(table)(\"name\", fn) — the callee is itself the `it.each(...)` call\n    return callee.type === \"CallExpression\" && isTestModifier(callee.callee);\n}\nfunction isExpectRootCall(node) {\n    return node.callee.type === \"Identifier\" && node.callee.name === \"expect\";\n}\nexport default {\n    meta: {\n        type: \"suggestion\",\n        docs: {\n            description: \"Enforce a maximum number of expect calls per it/test callback (default 1)\",\n        },\n        schema: [\n            {\n                type: \"object\",\n                properties: {\n                    max: { type: \"integer\", minimum: 1 },\n                },\n                additionalProperties: false,\n            },\n        ],\n        messages: {\n            tooManyExpects: \"Test has {{count}} expect calls (max {{max}}); assert one object with toEqual/toMatchObject or split the test\",\n        },\n    },\n    create(context) {\n        const max = context.options[0]?.max ?? 1;\n(eval):1: ==== not found","tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_a9cd0523b1d64c4181abbe9c","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

([validated by](test.ts#L42))`.\n * This rule inverts that view: it goes over each test declaration and fails the\n * ones that no spec or ADR statement references, so tests cannot silently drift\n * out of spec coverage.\n *\n * A test is linked when the spec/adr corpus carries a `([validated by](this#Lnn))`\n * link whose line falls inside the test's line span, or a whole-file link (no\n * `#L`) to the file. The corpus is read once per process (memoized per specsRoot)\n * via the shared parser — see `lib/spec-link-index.mjs`. Type info is off for\n * test files, so this works from the ESTree AST + filename + filesystem only.\n *\n * Detect-only: writing the link needs a human to pick which statement the test\n * validates, not a codemod.\n */\nimport path from \"node:path\";\nimport { isTestFile } from \"./lib/spec-parsers.mjs\";\nimport { buildLinkIndex, corpusExists, readSpecFiles, toPosix, } from \"./lib/spec-link-index.mjs\";\n/**\n * specsRoot+roots → index, so the corpus is walked once per process.\n *\n * Note: the cache is keyed on specsRoot only, with no mtime/content hash — a\n * single-pass `eslint`/CI run always reads fresh, but a long-lived ESLint\n * server (VS Code extension, --watch) will not see a spec link added after the\n * first lint until the server restarts.\n */\nconst indexCache = new Map();\n/** specsRoots we've already warned about having no spec/adr corpus, so a\n * misconfigured run warns once instead of once per linted test file.\n *\n * Scope is the whole Node process, matching `indexCache` above. In a one-shot\n * `eslint`/CI run that is exactly one warning. In a long-lived ESLint server\n * (VS Code, --watch) the module is not re-required between cycles, so once a\n * specsRoot has warned it stays quiet even after the CWD is fixed — the same\n * process-lifetime memoization caveat the corpus cache carries. Restart the\n * server (or the editor) to re-arm the warning. */\nconst warnedMissingCorpus = new Set();\nfunction getIndex(specsRoot, roots) {\n    // `\\0` separates every element so no root value can collide with the joiner.\n    const key = [specsRoot, ...roots].join(\"\\0\");\n    let index = indexCache.get(key);\n    if (!index) {\n        index = buildLinkIndex(readSpecFiles(specsRoot, roots));\n        indexCache.set(key, index);\n    }\n    return index;\n}\n/** The base identifier of a (possibly chained) callee — `it` in `it.each([])(…)`. */\nfunction rootCallName(callee) {\n    let node = callee;\n    while (node) {\n        if (node.type === \"Identifier\") {\n            return node.name;\n        }\n        if (node.type === \"MemberExpression\") {\n            node = node.object;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if (node.type === \"CallExpression\") {\n            node = node.callee;\n            continue;\n        }\n        // `it.each`table`(name, fn)` — the outer callee is a tagged template whose\n        // `.tag` is the `it.each` member chain; drill into it or the test escapes.\n        if (node.type === \"TaggedTemplateExpression\") {\n            node = node.tag;\n            continue;\n        }\n        return null;\n    }\n    return null;\n}\n/** A named test declaration: `it`/`test` (any modifier chain) with a string name. */\nfunction isNamedTestCall(node) {\n    const root = rootCallName(node.callee);\n    if (root !== \"it\" && root !== \"test\") {\n        return false;\n    }\n    const first = node.arguments[0];\n    if (!first) {\n        return false;\n    }\n    if (first.type === \"Literal\") {\n        return typeof first.value === \"string\";\n    }\n    return first.type === \"TemplateLiteral\";\n}\nfunction isLinked(entry, startLine, endLine) {\n    if (!entry) {\n        return false;\n    }\n    if (entry.wholeFile) {\n        return true;\n    }\n    for (const line of entry.lines) {\n        if (line >= startLine && line <= endLine) {\n            return true;\n        }\n    }\n    return false;\n}\n// With no corpus under specsRoot, every test would flag as unlinked — a\n// false-positive storm that means the run started outside the repo root\n// (e.g. `eslint apps/floor/` in a subdir). Warn once and skip rather than\n// report thousands of misleading errors.\nfunction warnMissingCorpusOnce(specsRoot, roots) {\n    if (warnedMissingCorpus.has(specsRoot)) {\n        return;\n    }\n    warnedMissingCorpus.add(specsRoot);\n    console.warn(`require-spec-link: no ${roots.join(\"/\")} directory under ${specsRoot} — ` +\n        \"run eslint from the repo root (or pass options.specsRoot). Skipping the spec-link check.\");\n}\nfunction testName(sourceCode, first) {\n    return first.type === \"Literal\"\n        ? {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_59b3228a40e2425bb1a8b215","type":"tool_result","content":"import {readFileSync} from 'node:fs';\nimport {dirname, basename, join} from 'node:path';\nimport {fileURLToPath} from 'node:url';\nimport eslint from '@eslint/js';\nimport markdown from '@eslint/markdown';\nimport reLint from '@re-cinq/eslint-plugin-re-lint';\nimport tseslint from 'typescript-eslint';\nimport {parse as parseYaml} from 'yaml';\n\n// layers.yaml is the readable declaration of the architecture; this hands it\n// to no-cross-layer-import.\n//\n// The rule keys packages by `<package>/src/`, which suits a monorepo of\n// packages and not a single package whose code sits at ./src. Left to find\n// layers.yaml itself the rule would resolve every file as `src/...`, match no\n// package, and report nothing - adopted in appearance, enforcing nothing. So\n// the entries are re-homed under this checkout's own directory name with the\n// root moved one level up, which is the shape the matcher expects.\n//\n// Paths come from this file's own URL rather than process.cwd(), so running\n// eslint from a subdirectory cannot silently disable the rule.\n// scripts/eslint-layers.test.ts fails if this ever stops reporting.\nconst repoRoot = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));\nconst declaredLayers = parseYaml(readFileSync(join(repoRoot, 'layers.yaml'), 'utf8')).layers.src;\n\n// Shared with eslint.config.backlog.mjs, which lints the same tree under the\n// two rules held out of the blocking gate. One list, so the two configs cannot\n// drift into disagreeing about what is even a source file.\n//\n// .claude/** is vendored agent tooling, maintained upstream rather than\n// here, so a change there must not be able to redden this repo's CI.\nexport const ignores = [\n  'node_modules/**',\n  'dist/**',\n  'coverage/**',\n  '.claude/**',\n  // Deliberately broken specs and ADRs - dead links, absent lead paragraphs,\n  // statuses no parser reads - kept as the fixtures the script tests assert\n  // against. Linting them would report the very faults they exist to reproduce.\n  'scripts/fixtures/**',\n];\n\nexport default tseslint.config(\n  {ignores},\n  {\n    // Scoped to TypeScript now that markdown is linted too: an unscoped block\n    // applies to every language, and JS rules do not survive a markdown AST.\n    files: ['**/*.ts'],\n    extends: [eslint.configs.recommended, ...tseslint.configs.recommended],\n    plugins: {'re-lint': reLint},\n    rules: {\n      // CLAUDE.md leads with five mandatory layers and \"no cross-layer\n      // shortcuts, no circular deps\". layers.yaml states that as data and this\n      // rule enforces it, so the architecture is a file someone can read rather\n      // than a habit that erodes.\n      're-lint/no-cross-layer-import': [\n        'error',\n        {root: dirname(repoRoot), layers: {[basename(repoRoot)]: declaredLayers}},\n      ],\n      '@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars': [\n        'error',\n        {\n          vars: 'all',\n          args: 'after-used',\n          argsIgnorePattern: '^_',\n          varsIgnorePattern: '^_',\n          caughtErrorsIgnorePattern: '^_',\n          ignoreRestSiblings: false,\n        },\n      ],\n      camelcase: 'error',\n      // CLAUDE.md: \"Tests live next to source: src/**/*.test.ts\". True of all\n      // ten test files today; this keeps it true.\n      're-lint/require-colocated-tests': 'error',\n      're-lint/no-commented-out-code': 'error',\n      // The provider layer must surface failures as AIError rather than\n      // swallowing them and fabricating a return value (CLAUDE.md, Adding a\n      // provider).\n      're-lint/no-catch-as-control-flow': 'error',\n      // Markdown is excluded because a doc quoting the code it documents is\n      // the intended state: README's example of createHalEngine and the\n      // interface blocks in specs/ are *supposed* to match src/. jscpd extracts\n      // fenced blocks and reports them as clones, so without this every\n      // accurate code sample is a lint error and the incentive is to let the\n      // docs drift. The same exclusion a jscpd config would carry; it lives\n      // here rather than in a .jscpd.json because the rule reads `ignore` from\n      // its own options and never from a config file.\n      're-lint/no-duplicate-code': ['error', {ignore: ['**/*.md']}],\n      're-lint/callee-below-caller': 'error',\n      're-lint/declare-near-use': 'error',\n      're-lint/default-export-matches-filename': 'error',\n      're-lint/max-boolean-operators': 'error',\n      're-lint/max-comment-lines': 'error',\n      're-lint/max-member-chain': 'error',\n      're-lint/no-closing-brace-comments': 'error',\n      're-lint/no-flag-params': 'error',\n      // INERT, kept as a placeholder. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_732fb96a11d145cbb2d5e642","type":"tool_result","content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Fails when a diff touches src/ and leaves CHANGELOG.md alone.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   bash scripts/check-changelog.sh [base-ref]     # default: origin/main\n#\n# The rule is about what a consumer can observe, not about effort: anything that\n# changes shipped behaviour needs a sentence they can read on npm. A change to\n# src/ that genuinely is not user-visible - an internal refactor, a test-only\n# edit - takes the `no-changelog` label instead, which is a deliberate, visible\n# act rather than a silent omission.\nset -uo pipefail\n\nbase=\"${1:-origin/main}\"\n\n# A base ref that does not resolve means nothing was compared. On a laptop that\n# is ordinary - a fresh clone has no origin/main - and skipping is right. In CI\n# it is the gate passing without running, which is the one outcome a gate must\n# never have, and it is exactly how a fetch that failed went unnoticed.\nif ! git rev-parse --verify --quiet \"$base\" >/dev/null; then\n  if [ -n \"${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}\" ]; then\n    echo \"check-changelog: FAILED - base ref '$base' does not resolve, so nothing was checked\" >&2\n    exit 1\n  fi\n  echo \"check-changelog: base ref '$base' not found; skipping\" >&2\n  exit 0\nfi\n\nmerge_base=\"$(git merge-base \"$base\" HEAD)\"\nchanged=\"$(git diff --name-only \"$merge_base\"..HEAD)\"\n\nsrc_changed=\"$(printf '%s\\n' \"$changed\" | grep -E '^src/' | grep -vE '\\.test\\.ts$' || true)\"\n\nif [ -z \"$src_changed\" ]; then\n  echo \"check-changelog: no shipped source changed since ${base}.\"\n  exit 0\nfi\n\nif printf '%s\\n' \"$changed\" | grep -qx 'CHANGELOG.md'; then\n  echo \"check-changelog: src/ changed and CHANGELOG.md was updated.\"\n  exit 0\nfi\n\n{\n  echo \"check-changelog: these files under src/ changed since ${base} and CHANGELOG.md did not:\"\n  printf '%s\\n' \"$src_changed\" | sed 's/^/  /'\n  echo\n  echo \"Add an entry under ## [Unreleased], written for somebody installing the package.\"\n  echo \"If the change genuinely is not user-visible, apply the 'no-changelog' label to the pull request.\"\n} >&2\nexit 1\n---\n# Changelog\n\nAll notable changes to `@re-cinq/hal-engine` are documented here.\n\nThe format is [Keep a Changelog 1.1.0](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres to\n[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html). Entries are written for somebody installing the\npackage, not for somebody reading this repository's commit log.\n\n## [Unreleased]\n\n### Added\n\n- `SessionStore` gains an optional `save(session)` member: the write signal a durable store needs. The engine calls it once per processed user message, from the same `finally` path that runs `afterSession`, so it fires for a turn that ended in a provider error as well as one that succeeded — a store that only heard about successes would lose exactly the conversations a customer complains about. By the time it runs, the turn's entries are committed, so the assistant entry's `isStreaming` is already `false` — including when a provider threw mid-stream, where the engine now closes the open entry before saving, recording `truncated` on it, rather than persisting a half-streamed entry that looks finished. An `afterSession` hook that throws no longer costs the turn its write signal. What `save` throws or rejects with is caught and logged as one line carrying the session id, and the turn continues: the client still receives its full stream and `stream_end`, because a database outage is not a reason for the agent to stop answering. The member is typed `void | Promise<void>`, so a synchronous implementation and an `async` one both satisfy it. Additive: `InMemorySessionStore` does not implement `save` and is unchanged, and a store that omits it behaves exactly as before.\n- `SessionStore` gains an optional `evict(sessionId)` member, and `InMemorySessionStore` implements it. The engine calls it only for a session whose socket closed while `create` was still pending — one that no client ever received and that has no entries to keep. `InMemorySessionStore` now also takes `{maxAgeMs}` (default `28_800_000`, eight hours), exported as `InMemorySessionStoreOptions`. Expired sessions are evicted when read and swept at the head of `create`, which stops at the first live session, so the bound costs nothing on a busy store. There is no timer: a library-owned interval would keep your process alive.\n- **`MongoSessionStore`**, a durable session store, exported as `MongoSessionStore` and `createMongoSessionStore`. It takes a collection, a client with a database name, or a connection URL — nothing in the package reads the environment or assumes a host. The collection is the truth and the in-process cache is an optimisation: a session written by `save` is readable by a second store on the same collection. `delete` removes the document — it is the consumer's erasure primitive and the engine never calls it — as do `eraseConversation`, `eraseOlderThan(cutoff)` and `eraseAll`, while `clear` alone touches only the cache; `docs/session-stores.md` opens with the table that says which is which, because the previous documentation would have led you to believe `delete` erased. Documents carry `createdAt` and `updatedAt`, so a retention period is expressible without per-entry timestamps. **No credential is ever written**: `authHeaders`, `authorization`, `cookie` and `host` are stripped at any depth, not just the top level, and the same `stripCredentialKeys` is exported for stores you write yourself. `mongodb` is an optional peer dependency loaded only when the store actually connects, so a consumer who installs no optional peer can still import the package root and use the in-memory store. **Migration note**: `delete` and `evict` both erase on this store, so the one-line `onDisconnect: sessionId => store.delete(sessionId)` that restores the pre-0.4 close behaviour destroys the conversation on every socket close — point `onDisconnect` at neither. Nothing needs reclaiming by hand: the in-process cache is bounded by `maxAgeMs` (eight hours by default) and drops stale entries without touching a document. This does **not** deliver conversation resume, and it does not make the engine safe to run as more than one instance against one conversation.\n\n### Changed\n\n- Every `SessionStore` member is now `Awaitable<T>` (`T | Promise<T>`) rather than a bare `T`, so a store backed by a database is expressible for the first time. `Awaitable` is exported from the package root. **A synchronous implementation needs no change** — `T` is assignable to `T | Promise<T>` in a return position — and `InMemorySessionStore` is unedited. The WebSocket connection handler now awaits `create` and the release that follows a close: it pauses the socket across the await so a frame sent before `connected` arrives is buffered rather than dropped, attaches its `close` listener before the await so a socket that closes mid-create leaves no session behind, and catches a rejection from either call so one store failure closes one socket instead of ending the process with an unhandled rejection. **Migration note**: the `connected` frame now arrives one tick later, after the awaited `create`, so a client that waits for it (as the protocol already requires) sees no difference; only code that assumed the frame was emitted synchronously with the upgrade does.\n- **The engine no longer erases a conversation when its socket closes.** The WebSocket close handler called `sessionStore.delete(sessionId)` unconditionally, which meant that behind a durable store every conversation was written and then destroyed the moment the customer closed their tab — the opposite of what this engine's own documentation promised. `SessionStore.delete` now has no engine-internal caller at all and is purely your erasure primitive. The credentials the socket carried are cleared from the session on close, since they were issued for a request that is over; the entries are untouched. **Migration note**: to restore the old behaviour exactly, pass `onDisconnect: sessionId => store.delete(sessionId)` — that one line is the whole migration. If you rely on the default store not growing, note that it is now bounded by `maxAgeMs` (eight hours) rather than by the close handler; that is a memory bound, not a retention policy, and the retention decision remains yours.\n\n## [0.3.0] - 2026-09-29\n\n**Upgrading from 0.2.x.** Nothing is removed and no existing signature changes, but check these before you bump:\n\n- `OrchestratorHooks` gains two optional members, `beforeToolCall` and `onToolBudgetExhausted`. Code that checks the hooks exhaustively, for example `satisfies Record<keyof OrchestratorHooks, …>`, fails to type-check until it names both.\n- `ToolRegistry.execute` now validates tool input against each tool's `inputSchema`, so a tool that produced its own message for malformed input receives only valid input; the model reads the registry's validation message instead.\n- `maxToolRounds` now counts executed rounds: the default of 5 runs 5 tool rounds, not 6. Raise it by one to keep the old count.\n- Offering a bare access token as the only WebSocket subprotocol still works but is deprecated: offer `hal.v1` beside it now, because the next minor release stops accepting a bare token.\n- New dependencies: `ajv`, and `cookie` moves from `^0.7` to `^2`.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"413e4093-822e-4255-a152-2fb521364e6e","uuid":"79b7eada-94dc-473f-b9f9-837a53a652cb","timestamp":"2026-11-01T01:42:03.117Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Fails when a diff touches src/ and leaves CHANGELOG.md alone.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   bash scripts/check-changelog.sh [base-ref]     # default: origin/main\n#\n# The rule is about what a consumer can observe, not about effort: anything that\n# changes shipped behaviour needs a sentence they can read on npm. {createChatOrchestrator} from './chatOrchestrator.js';\nimport type {OrchestratorHooks} from './chatOrchestrator.js';\nimport type {AIProvider, MessageChunk, SendMessageParams} from '../types/ai.js';\nimport type {ChatSession} from '../types/session.js';\nimport {PromptBuilder} from '../infrastructure/builders/promptBuilder.js';\n\n// Fixed so a rerun cannot read the clock; nothing asserts on it.\nconst SENT_AT = '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z';\n\nconst promptBuilder = new PromptBuilder({identity: 'You are a test assistant.'});\n\n// One expect per test needs the rejection as a value rather than a matcher.\nconst outcomeOf = (call: Promise<unknown>): Promise<string> =>\n  call.then(() => 'resolved without throwing').catch((error: Error) => error.message);\n\nconst sessionFor = (content: string): ChatSession => ({\n  sessionId: 'hook-failure-s1',\n  userId: 'hook-failure-u1',\n  entries: [{role: 'user', content, timestamp: SENT_AT}],\n});\n\n// Counts sendMessage invocations, so a test can show the model was never reached.\nconst countingProvider = (): {provider: AIProvider; calls: () => number} => {\n  let sent = 0;\n\n  return {\n    calls: () => sent,\n    provider: {\n      async *sendMessage(_params: SendMessageParams): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n        sent++;\n        yield {type: 'text', text: 'unreachable'};\n        yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn'};\n      },\n      async generateStructured<T>(): Promise<T> {\n        return {} as T;\n      },\n    },\n  };\n};\n\ndescribe('beforeSession failure (issue #94)', () => {\n  it('routes a beforeSession throw through onError and afterSession and still rejects', async () => {\n    const thrown = new Error('span allocation failed');\n    const session = sessionFor('hello');\n    const order: string[] = [];\n    let onErrorSession: ChatSession | undefined;\n    let onErrorError: unknown;\n    const hooks: OrchestratorHooks = {\n      beforeSession: async () => {\n        order.push('beforeSession');\n        throw thrown;\n      },\n      onError: async (hookSession, error) => {\n        order.push('onError');\n        onErrorSession = hookSession;\n        onErrorError = error;\n      },\n      afterSession: async () => {\n        order.push('afterSession');\n      },\n    };\n\n    const {provider} = countingProvider();\n    const orchestrator = createChatOrchestrator(provider, promptBuilder, undefined, {hooks});\n    const outcome = await outcomeOf(orchestrator.processMessage(session));\n\n    expect({\n      outcome,\n      order,\n      sawSameSession: onErrorSession === session,\n      sawSameError: onErrorError === thrown,\n    }).toEqual({\n      outcome: 'span allocation failed',\n      order: ['beforeSession', 'onError', 'afterSession'],\n      sawSameSession: true,\n      sawSameError: true,\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('hands afterSession a session the failed turn never started', async () => {\n    const session = sessionFor('hello');\n    const {provider, calls} = countingProvider();\n    let afterSessionCalls = 0;\n    let entriesSeenInHook = -1;\n    const hooks: OrchestratorHooks = {\n      beforeSession: async () => {\n        throw new Error('span allocation failed');\n      },\n      afterSession: async hookSession => {\n        afterSessionCalls++;\n        entriesSeenInHook = hookSession.entries.length;\n      },\n    };\n\n    const orchestrator = createChatOrchestrator(provider, promptBuilder, undefined, {hooks});\n    const outcome = await outcomeOf(orchestrator.processMessage(session));\n\n    expect({\n      outcome,\n      afterSessionCalls,\n      entriesSeenInHook,\n      entriesAfterTurn: session.entries.length,\n      providerCalls: calls(),\n    }).toEqual({\n      outcome: 'span allocation failed',\n      afterSessionCalls: 1,\n      entriesSeenInHook: 1,\n      entriesAfterTurn: 1,\n      providerCalls: 0,\n    });\n  });\n});\n"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":0},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"413e4093-822e-4255-a152-2fb521364e6e","uuid":"a4b36af4-cf45-4aaf-8c42-19948ced43af","timestamp":"2026-11-01T01:43:19.375Z"}
